{"redo_booking_notes":"Please ensure you review/complete the following documents:

River Indemnity (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1vx60K4WhmatAmR_YPPFaI2pDw2msXQjh/edit)

HIKING PACKING AND EQUIPMENT LIST (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DwLK66TQ-oQFFy3Vp3vYxZlYUlh7g56H/edit)

CANOEING PACKING AND EQUIPMENT LIST (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RTWtoOnlmAo-v8QZtX4MBniTURBVYnmu/edit)

HIRE CAR:
Hire a car in Darwin, travel directly here or through Kakadu on the way. Your vehicle can be left safely at our premises while you are out on tour and then it is there ready waiting for you when you return.

GREYHOUND BUSES:
A Daily service from Darwin to Katherine is available. One way ticket between $65 & $90 per person.
Phone: 13 14 99

For any of these forms of transport, arriving a few days early is always an option with many interesting things to do and see around Katherine.

WHERE TO STAY:

MANBULLOO STATION HOMESTEAD AND CARAVAN PARK:
Manbulloo Homestead is a unique hideaway rural retreat located on the banks of the tranquil Katherine River. It is a traditional working cattle property with much historic value in the region. Motel rooms link onto a communal kitchen and self contained cabins are also available. It has a caravan park with shady, well grassed sites with free BBQ use. (Please note: there is no restaurant or food purchase facilities at Manbulloo)

Guests enjoy bush-walking and bird-watching along the river and some try their hand at fishing and catching fresh-water prawn - Pets are also welcome!

Motel rooms (renovated station visitors quarters)

Nestled in lush tropical gardens complete with spa are three rooms catering for from one to four people. These rooms share a well appointed shower / toilet and a large fully equipped kitchen. They are air-conditioned and have a fridge and television.

Cabins:
Built on stilts, facing the Katherine River is an ideal setting for our air-conditioned fully self contained cabins capable of sleeping four people. The verandah faces the lush vegetation along the river, only 100m away

Cost: Single $105pn, Double $115pn, Extra adult/child $15pn (may alter)

In Katherine (Pick-up service offered)

Paraway Motel:
The Paraway has a range of well priced accommodation to 3 Star Motel rooms. It is located just quietly on the edge of the township and has a nice pool, bar and restaurant

Contact: (08) 8972 2644 OR 1800 222 511 (mention Gecko)

Pick up service is available for all Katherine based Motels.

Alternative Accommodation in the Region.

PLEASE NOTE: We don’t offer a pick-up service from these venues. So it is best that you have your own vehicle.

At Nitmiluk (32kms from town)

Phone: 1300 146 743 or email: kathshop@nitmiluktours.com.au

TENT VILLAGE:
For travelers on a budget Nitmiluk offers a Tent Village package. The sites are centrally positioned in the campground just 600m to the departure point for boat cruises and canoes. Your budget-style tent is ready upon arrival, tents are complete with camp-style beds and linen. Hot showers and toilets are nearby. A delicious takeaway dinner is included in the price, which can be had by the landscaped pool.

NITMILUK CHALETS:
Self contained accommodation. The Nitmiluk chalets are centrally positioned below the escarpment entrance just 600 metres to the departure point for boat cruises, canoes and several short circuit walks. Includes a balcony, where wallabies and other wildlife can be observed wandering freely. They are also near the resort style pool.

Children 0 to 12 years - free when sharing with an adult and using existing bedding. Max capacity 1 Bedroom - 2, 2 Bedroom - 5.

ACCOMMODATION FEATURES: Air-conditioning, Balcony, Full cooking facilities

Refrigerator, Tea/coffee making facilities, Internet access (broadband),

Flat Screen Television, Satellite TV, Room serviced daily

CICADA LODGE:
A new 4-5 star lodge in Nitmiluk Park. www.cicadalodge.com.au

THINGS TO DO IN AND AROUND KATHERINE:

KATHERINE VISITOR INFORMATION CENTRE:
Information on Katherine Tours, Attractions, Accommodation, Dining and much more.
visitkatherine.com.au

NITMILUK (KATHERINE) GORGE:
A Top End Icon, a must see. Board a cruise boat for an unforgettable experience through the gorges. Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner cruises as well as the standard 2 & 4 hour cruises, canoe hire and caravan/camping facilities available.
Phone: 1300 146 743 or email: kathshop@nitmiluktours.com.au

Please Call 24-48hrs prior to advise us of your arrival and final accommodation details.

Please ensure that we are advised of any special dietary/medical requirements via the pre-sent BOOKING forms at least 14 days prior to the tour, ensuring details of any irregular medical conditions, dietary requirements and swimming ability. If applicable – You will require spare medications to compensate for unforeseen circumstances if they arise.

As we operate in a remote area, we are often isolated from immediate professional medical assistance. Your guide has remote area incident management training and will need to know of any irregular medical conditions in case of a potential emergency.

If you require Asprin, Panadol, anti histamine or anti inflammatory drugs, please bring with you, as we are not permitted to supply on tour (headaches, allergic reactions, swelling from insect bites or swollen joints, etc).

Please be aware that we will pass through areas which MAY be inhabited by crocodilis porosis (Estuarine/Salt water crocodiles). Your guide/s are experienced and aware of locations and procedures for safe touring, (including safe swimming).

Don’t forget to bring your favourite wine and spirits (River Trips). Beer and soft drinks cannot be kept cold. Please note that alcohol sales in Katherine are between 2pm and 8pm.

Please leave your jewellery at home, necklaces, bracelets and rings have been lost on the river in the past!!

Please advise us if you are driving and you need to store a vehicle with us, as arrangements will be made to meet at our depot at Manbulloo Homestead on the morning of the tour.

WHERE TO STAY:
Gecko Canoeing and Trekking Tours depart in the mornings from our riverside base at Manbulloo Station. Our pick up service is offered here.
Call: (08) 8972 1559 email: manbulloohs@bigpond.com.au (mention Gecko)
Through Website: www.manbulloohomesteadcaravanpark.com.au/contact
MANBULLOO STATION HOMESTEAD AND CARAVAN PARK:
Manbulloo Homestead is a unique hideaway rural retreat located on the banks of the tranquil Katherine River. It is a traditional working cattle property with much historic value in the region. Motel rooms link onto a communal kitchen and self contained cabins are also available. It has a caravan park with shady, well grassed sites with free BBQ use. (Please note: there is no restaurant or food purchase facilities at Manbulloo)
Guests enjoy bush-walking and bird-watching along the river and some try their hand at fishing and catching fresh-water prawn - Pets are also welcome!
Motel rooms (renovated station visitors quarters):
Nestled in lush tropical gardens complete with spa are three rooms catering for from one to four people. These rooms share a well appointed shower / toilet and a large fully equipped kitchen. They are air-conditioned and have a fridge and television.
Cabins:
Built on stilts, facing the Katherine River is an ideal setting for our air-conditioned fully self contained cabins capable of sleeping four people. The verandah faces the lush vegetation along the river, only 100m away
Cost: Single $105pn, Double $115pn, Extra adult/child $15pn (may alter)
In Katherine (Pick-up service offered):
Paraway Motel:
The Paraway has a range of well priced accommodation to 3 Star Motel rooms. It is located just quietly on the edge of the township and has a nice pool, bar and restaurant
Contact: (08) 8972 2644 OR 1800 222 511 (mention Gecko)
Pick up service is available for all Katherine based Motels.

You can buy singular lessons, or for an even better deal, you can buy a Package Deal and receive multiple lessons at a discount rate (For individual surfers only).

Intermediate Classes (Option 2): Intermediate classes will focus on riding unbroken waves, how to get through the waves properly, correct positioning to catch unbroken waves, how to turn and ride across the wave, advance pop up techniques and much more! These classes are suitable for students who have taken at least 2-3 beginner classes, had some practise by them selves and are feeling confident with their pop up in white water.

x3 beginner lessons alongside some practise rentals
x3 intermediate classes alongside some practise rentals

2 hours of expert instruction from qualified Surfing NZ Instructors

Receive 50% off a Moana Rd hooded towel with every board or wetsuit purchase!
Just text the team on 0211764073 to receive this offer!

The app is also where you’ll:
Access your Advanced Adventurer digital learning materials
Log your dives during and after the course
Track your certifications and training progress.

The Advanced Adventurer course is completed over 3–4 days, and can be scheduled flexibly across weekends or combined with other boat trips, depending on availability. The course includes:
E-learning via your MySSI account
5 adventure dives from a selection of specialties

Boat Diving

{"redo_booking_notes":"Thanks for choosing this Great Alpine & Lakes winter adventure with WAM! We can't wait for you to join us on a spectacular journey into the Victorian Alps and Gippsland Lakes.

As one of Australia's only certified tour operator B-Corps, just by booking with us, you have done a lot of good for the planet, congratulations! (read on for more details of how)

Before we do so, please take a minute to read some important information about the trip:

For our Great Alpine & Lakes Adventure, we require a minimum of 5 people for the trip to run. If the trip does not reach minimum numbers, we will inform you at least 60 days prior to the trip and you will be provided with a full refund of what you have paid.
The balance of the trip is due 60 days before departure.
You’ll start receiving emails as we get closer to the date with information about the trip, what to bring etc.
Once you have the date confirmed, if you need to cancel, we require a minimum 60 days notice to provide a refund (less your deposit)

Pick up Location:
We will have 3 pick-up locations on the day of departure.
Mornington Peninsula
Frankston
Melbourne CBD
We will provide further details on these closer to the date.

Premium Service:
To maximise your comfort we provide you with an eco-pack for the trip which includes products from Australian businesses that directly support the environment. This includes a reusable water bottle, keep-cup, reef-safe sunscreen, sunscreen and a towel. You simply hand these back at the end of your experience. Its a bit like a pack you may get on a first class flight or a luxury hotel, except ours is good for the planet!

Now for the deep and meaningful:
By booking an adventure with us you have directly helped make a long-term positive environmental and social impact by:

Donating a portion of everything booking to Zoos Victoria to support the Mountain Pygmy Possum (and other endangered species), these little guys were thought to be extinct until being discovered in a loft in Hotham in the 1960's. Critically endangered, Mountain Pygmy Possums are Australia's only hibernating marsupial so will be sleeping while we are on the slopes above, knowing we have supported the conservation of this very special species.
Planting native trees on the Mornington Peninsula with MP Koalas to capture carbon emissions, protect our climate, enhance soil and water quality, and restore habitat for native wildlife.
Regenerate reefs and native kelp locally with The Nature Conservancy, providing marine habitat, filtering seawater, removing nitrogen and phosphate, and preventing used shell from entering landfill.
Support female education with The Stars Foundation which empowers and supports Indigenous young women and girls to complete education and find work.
Protect and plant mangroves to protect our coastlines, wildlife and support blue carbon projects.

You'll find additional information relevant to your adventure on the Wild Adventures Melbourne website. Please check the website for exactly what items we recommend bringing with you on the day.

Green is our Gold Commitment:

As members of Australia's tourism industry, we believe a land as precious
as ours should be preserved for generations to come. As a visitor, we ask that you do the same. That’s why we’ve set some unwritten rules that have kept our backyard beautiful for thousands of years.

Passed down through story and practice, they’re how we walk gently, listen deeply, tread with care – and look out for each other along the way.

By following them throughout your visit, you too can care for Australia when you Come and say G’day.

Consider these principles a bit of local knowledge. A few fundamentals to help you respect this place and have an unforgettable stay in the process.

The Guiding Principles:
Celebrate Community: The best part of an Australian visit is the people you meet. Shop local, engage with communities, and you’ll leave with new mates aplenty.
Embrace Culture: Australia’s cultural diversity stretches from ancient songlines to city laneways. Immerse yourself in it all - honour First Nations cultures, embrace our diversity, and you’ll leave with new knowledge and new friends.
Preserve Place: In Australia you’ll find some of the most unspoilt landscapes on Earth. Help keep them that way by minimising your impact wherever you go.
Respect Wildlife: Australia has some of the most unique animals on the planet. Take as many photos as you like but remember to give them space and respect their homes.
Take Care: We look out for one another in Australia, but it’s important to take care of yourself too. Listen to the land, respect it, and always put safety first.

If you have any questions between now and your trip with us, please don't hesitate to email or call me directly.","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"Equipment hire and lessons - Mount Hotham: We can help arrange equipment hire and lessons at Mount Hotham if required so please contact us for further details.","redo_booking_meeting_point":"","redo_booking_check_in":"","redo_booking_before_arrival":"","redo_booking_departure_info":"","redo_booking_itinerary":"","redo_booking_duration_text":"","redo_booking_important_info":"","redo_booking_health_safety":"","redo_booking_restrictions":"","redo_booking_special_requirements":"","redo_booking_accessibility":"","redo_booking_group_size":"","redo_booking_cancellation":"","redo_booking_disclaimers":"","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":"Sign-off omitted: Looking forward to adventuring with you soon,

{"redo_booking_notes":"Cellar Doors:
Your day is your own where you have the freedom to pick and choose who you want to visit 
but don't worry about doing too much planning in advance as we will be here to help you on the day with lots of up-to-date information about the cellar doors, as well as heaps of friendly advice about how you can make the most of your day, too. 😊

There are upwards of 14+ beautiful cellar doors who are more than happy for you to visit them for a tasting without the need to book an appointment in advance, however, there are some exceptions to this rule:-
Cloudy Bay: (a 40 minute bike ride from our base)
Hunters: (a 40 minute bike ride from our base)
Hans Herzog: (a 20 minute bike ride from our base)
Framingham Wines: (a 10 minute bike ride from our base)

If any of these 4 cellar doors are on your bucket list, just head to their websites to find their booking forms. With Cloudy Bay and Hunters being 40 minutes away, we would recommend you make a booking between 12 Noon -1pm so that you get the big bike ride out of the way at the start of the day when you are nice and fresh, then you can work your way back and be close to home at the end of the day. 😊 

There are some cellar doors that we feel are too far away to get to on a bike, or that the roads to reach them are just not safe - Clos Henri, Saint Clair's, Wither Hills, Lawsons Dry Hills - we feel these are best visited by car.

For groups over 8+ pax - the cellar doors do ask that we book you in and we will work with you and help put together a personalized itinerary and get spots secured at the cellar doors for you.

Cheese & Mixed Platters:
Most of the cellar doors have platter food available for purchase if you wish to have something to nibble on alongside your tastings. These can be ordered when you arrive at the cellar door.

Restaurants:
Bookings are recommended and we are always here to help if you are not sure what time to book😊
Vines Village Café: 20 minutes biking from our base (Open 7 days a week).
The Fancy Cow: 25 minutes biking from our base (Open 6 days, closed on Mondays)
Allan Scott: 40 minutes biking from our base – bookings essential - (Open 7 days a week)
Number 11 at Wairau River: 15 minutes biking from our base - (Open 7 days a week as of 7th November 2024)

Note: Wither Hills and Saint Clair’s restaurants are not accessible on our bikes - they are too far away and the roads are not safe getting to them - we feel they are best visited by car :-)

For those on the Roadsters:
These bikes need to stay on the bike paths and quiet roads, so the beautiful cellar doors you can visit are...
Gibson Bridge
Forrest Wines: - platters available for purchase
Framingham Wines: - "build your own platter" - food available for purchase
Nautilus Estate: - platter food available for purchase
Bladen: - food truck & platters food available for purchase (closed on Wednesdays)
Boomtown Beer Garden: - food truck (Open Thurs-Sun as of 1st November 2024)
Number 11 at Wairau River: - restaurant and tasting room (Open 7 days a week as of 7th November 2024)

We are really looking forward to seeing you but if you have any questions before you arrive, please just ask away as we are always here to help :-)

10 Inkerman Street, Renwick, Marlborough
Calling on a NZ Phone - 03 572 7954 or 027 249 5646
Calling using an International Phone - (+64) 3 572 7954 or (+64) 27 249 5646
Email - info@winetoursbybike.co.nz
Web - www.winetoursbybike.co.nz

{"redo_booking_notes":"Thanks for choosing your adventure with WAM! We can't wait for you to join us on a spectacular journey into nature.

Just by booking with us, you have done a lot of good for the planet, congratulations! (read on for more details of how)

Before we do so, please take a minute to read some important information about your tour:

WAM Adventures require a minimum of 4 people to run. We almost always run our trips but we'll be in contact as we get closer to the date for updates.
You’ll start receiving emails as we get closer to the date.
Once you have a date confirmed, if you need to cancel, we require a minimum 7 days notice to provide a refund (please read our T&C's for other options)

Gift vouchers: If you have a gift voucher, you'll need to redeem it at some stage by returning to the relevant tour page, selecting a date and entering the voucher code at the checkout - think of your voucher as like a pre-paid credit card
Also, we can’t extend the use-by date on gift vouchers past three years (three years is pretty good!)

Premium Service: We include everything you need on your adventure including activities, equipment, food and refreshments.
To maximise your comfort we even provide you with eco-pack for the day which includes some special products from local businesses that directly support the environment. This includes free sunscreen and a towel service. You simply hand these back at the end of your experience. Its a bit like a pack you may get on a first class flight or a luxury hotel, except ours is good for the planet!

Now for the deep and meaningful:
By booking an adventure with us you have directly helped make a long-term positive environmental and social impact by:
Planting native trees on the Mornington Peninsula with MP Koalas to capture carbon emissions, protect our climate, enhance soil and water quality, and restore habitat for native wildlife.
Regenerate reefs and native kelp locally with The Nature Conservancy, providing marine habitat, filtering seawater, removing nitrogen and phosphate, and preventing used shell from entering landfill.
Support female education with The Stars Foundation which empowers and supports Indigenous young women and girls to complete education and find work.
Protect and plant mangroves to protect our coastlines, wildlife and support blue carbon projects.

You'll find additional information relevant to your adventure on the Wild Adventures Melbourne website. Please check the website for exactly what items we recommend bringing with you on the day.

Green is our Gold Commitment:
As members of Australia’s tourism industry, we believe a land as precious
as ours should be preserved for generations to come. As a visitor, we ask that you do the same. That’s why we’ve set some unwritten rules that have kept our backyard beautiful for thousands of years.

Passed down through story and practice, they’re how we walk gently, listen deeply, tread with care – and look out for each other along the way.

By following them throughout your visit, you too can care for Australia when you Come and say G’day.

Consider these principles a bit of local knowledge. A few fundamentals to help you respect this place and have an unforgettable stay in the process.

The Guiding Principles:
Celebrate Community: The best part of an Australian visit is the people you meet.
Shop local, engage with communities, and you’ll leave with new mates aplenty.

Embrace Culture: Australia’s cultural diversity stretches from ancient songlines to city laneways. Immerse yourself in it all - honour First Nations cultures, embrace our diversity, and you’ll leave with new knowledge and new friends.

Preserve Place: In Australia you’ll find some of the most unspoilt landscapes on Earth. Help keep them that way by minimising your impact wherever you go.

Respect Wildlife: Australia has some of the most unique animals on the planet. Take as many photos as you like but remember to give them space and respect their homes.

Take Care: We look out for one another in Australia, but it’s important to take care of yourself too. Listen to the land, respect it, and always put safety first.

If you have any questions between now and your trip with us, please don't hesitate to email or call me directly.","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"Pick up Location: We meet on the Mornington Peninsula at Devilbend Natural Features Reserve, 159 Graydens Rd, Moorooduc VIC 3933. {"redo_booking_notes":"Cellar Doors: Your day is your own where you have the freedom to pick and choose who you want to visit 
but don't panic about doing too much planning in advance as we will be here to help you on the day with lots of up-to-date information about the cellar doors, as well as heaps of friendly advice about them all, too. 😊

There are upwards of 14+ beautiful cellar doors who are more than happy for you to visit them for a tasting without the need to book an appointment in advance, however, there are some exceptions to this rule:-
Cloudy Bay (a 40 minute bike ride from our base)
Hunters (a 40 minute bike ride from our base)
Hans Herzog (a 20 minute bike ride from our base)
Framingham Wines (a 10 minute bike ride from our base)

If any of these 4 cellar doors are on your bucket list, just head to their websites to find their booking forms. With Cloudy Bay and Hunters being 40 minutes away, we would recommend you make a booking between 12 Noon -1pm so that you get the big bike ride out of the way at the start of the day when you are nice and fresh, then work your way back so you are close to home at the end. 😊

Q: I have allergies/dietary requirements. Will this be catered for? A: If you have dietary requirements that are generally more common ie lactose intolerant, vegetarian, gluten free, allergic to nuts or shellfish etc, we will advise the restaurant and they will cater to your specific requirements.

If you have requirements that are little more uncommon, please advise us in advance so we can liaise with the restaurant to confirm your requirements.

We will always try our best to cater for all dietary requirements. No request is too big or too small. If you are unsure, please contact us for further details.

PLEASE NOTE: A vegan lunch can be ordered, but the chocolate, cheese and most wine is not vegan. Those on a strict vegan diet CANNOT be catered for on our regular public tour.
Q: Why do I need closed toe shoes? A: Our tour goes behind the scenes on a production tour of a winery. Closed toe shoes are a requirement of entry to the production area.
Q: What days do you operate the public Hunter Valley wine tours? A: Generally, public Hunter Valley wine tours operate daily except public holidays and Christmas Eve, Melbourne Cup Day and New Years Eve, but are subject to minimum number requirements.

Before we do so, please take a minute to read some important information about your tour:
- If you need to cancel, we require a minimum 7 days notice to provide a refund (please read our T&C's for other options)
Please check in and sign the waiver prior to the date of your adventure.

Also, we can’t extend the use-by date on gift vouchers past three years (three years is pretty good!)

Now for the deep and meaningful:
By booking an adventure with us you have directly helped make a long-term positive environmental and social impact by:
- Planting native trees on the Mornington Peninsula with MP Koalas to capture carbon emissions, protect our climate, enhance soil and water quality, and restore habitat for native wildlife.
- Regenerate reefs and native kelp locally with The Nature Conservancy, providing marine habitat, filtering seawater, removing nitrogen and phosphate, and preventing used shell from entering landfill.
- Support female education with The Stars Foundation which empowers and supports Indigenous young women and girls to complete education and find work.
- Protect and plant mangroves to protect our coastlines, wildlife and support blue carbon projects.

You'll find additional information relevant to your adventure on the Wild Adventures Melbourne website. Please check the website for exactly what items we recommend bringing with you on the day.

Green is our Gold Commitment:

As members of Australia’s tourism industry, we believe a land as precious
as ours should be preserved for generations to come. As a visitor, we ask that you do the same. That’s why we’ve set some unwritten rules that have kept our backyard beautiful for thousands of years.

Passed down through story and practice, they’re how we walk gently, listen deeply, tread with care – and look out for each other along the way. 

By following them throughout your visit, you too can care for Australia when you Come and say G’day.

Consider these principles a bit of local knowledge. A few fundamentals to help you respect this place and have an unforgettable stay in the process.

The Guiding Principles:

Celebrate Community: The best part of an Australian visit is the people you meet.
Shop local, engage with communities, and you’ll leave with new mates aplenty.

Embrace Culture: Australia’s cultural diversity stretches from ancient songlines to city laneways. Immerse yourself in it all - honour First Nations cultures, embrace our diversity, and you’ll leave with new knowledge and new friends.

Preserve Place: In Australia you’ll find some of the most unspoilt landscapes on Earth. Help keep them that way by minimising your impact wherever you go.

Respect Wildlife: Australia has some of the most unique animals on the planet. Take as many photos as you like but remember to give them space and respect their homes.

Take Care: We look out for one another in Australia, but it’s important to take care of yourself too. Listen to the land, respect it, and always put safety first.

Time: 9:30am – 3:00pm
Please arrive 10–15 minutes early so we can begin on time.

How to safely process household food scraps
How to feed a thriving worm farm
How to avoid common composting problems
How to use worm compost to improve garden health and fertility
You'll also receive a 250ml Effective Microbes (EM) starter solution to help you get started at home.
For those who have purchased the optional starter pack, we'll have this ready for collection on the day.

Q: What are my transport/parking options getting to the event? A: Barangaroo Reserve is easily accessible by public transport and on foot from Walsh Bay, Millers Point and The Rocks. The closest stations are Barangaroo Metro, Wynyard and Circular Quay train stations. For further information about getting to Barangaroo visit here.

If driving, there is a 300-space carpark underneath the park, accessed via Towns Place and operated by Wilson Parking. Find details here
Accessibility: Barangaroo Reserve is a place for everyone and our aim is to make it accessible to all visitors, of all ages, including those with additional mobility requirements. Learn more here.
Q: Are there toilets at Barangaroo Reserve? A: Toilets are in two locations within Barangaroo Reserve.

There are toilets inside the heritage 1904 Pump House at Marrinawi Cove, near the Towns Place entrance in Millers Point. Baby change and accessible toilets are located there.

There are toilets, including baby change and accessible toilets, on the ground floor main lobby of the Cutaway. The entrance is at the Hickson Road entrance to Barangaroo Reserve. The Cutaway toilets are accessible via the car park lift or from Wulugul Walk at Nawi Cove. (Note: Cutaway toilets are currently closed while it is being redeveloped. They will reopen with the Cutaway)
Q: Is there a cafe at Barangaroo Reserve? A: Not yet. Cafes and bars are open at Barangaroo's southern precinct. It is advisable to pack snacks and bring a drink bottle - drinking fountains are available throughout the park.
Q: What is the refund policy? A: All sales are final.
Q: What is your weather policy? A: Tours will proceed in all weather conditions. It is recommended you bring clothing for all weather conditions, including sun, wind and rain protection. In the event of extreme weather such as electrical storms, high winds or extreme heat, tours may be postponed and participants advised accordingly.
Q: What are the terms of concession tickets? A: Concession tickets require student or pensioner ID cards with a concession ID. Student Concessions are only issued to full-time students – a student ID card does not suffice. Seniors Cards are considered concession cards.
Whilst photography is welcomed during a tour experience filming or audio recording of tour content without prior consent is strictly prohibited.","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":""}

{"redo_booking_notes":"Thank you for joining Sydney Kayak on a Pittwater Lunch Paddle with Waterfall bush walk.
Your guide for this adventure is Sam Mcleod
What to expect:
You will be paddling on beautiful Pittwater. You will see Australian Bush and Water access only homes.
This is a medium paddle of about an hour and a half each way depending on conditions and the paddling ability of the group.
The walk to the Lovett bay waterfall a bit steep, but not too bad if you have a medium level of fitness.
The Walk is approx 1km return. The Waterfall lookout is approx 100m above Sea level, so its a bit of a climb. No problem for the able-bodied, but quite steep so not suitable for those with bad knees or the unfit.
Any questions or issues call Sam on 04 5188 7675","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"You should bring water and a change of clothes for after the paddle in case you get wet.
It is rare for anyone to fall in but you can get damp from paddle splash.
You can bring phones and Cameras but remember there is a risk as they don’t float and usually don’t work if dropped in water.
For anything with a touch screen it is a good idea to have a small cloth to wipe drops from wet fingers off the screen as they can be sensed as a finger touch and make use difficult.
Anything you don’t want to get wet should be in a zip lock bag as a minimum.
There is some room in the Kayak for small items.
There is no room for large items such as backpacks so it is recommended that they are left in the car.
Paddling is a water sport so expect to get splashed.
Your feet will get wet.
Footwear is strongly recommended and should be suitable for the bushwalk, as well as being in the Water.
Alternatively you can bring paddle shoes and bushwalking shoes.
The clothing Golden Rules - your kayak clothing should:
NO COTTON or DENIM - when it gets wet, it does not dry and remains cold and heavy!
When wet, your clothing must stay warm AND dry quickly!
The key concept to bear in mind is layering. Several thin garments will keep you just as warm as a single thicker one, and are much more versatile.
Remember you’ll need to think about staying cool as much as staying warm, and you can always add or subtract layers.
A light Nylon Jacket will keep out wind and water. Fleeces are OK. {"redo_booking_notes":"","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"","redo_booking_check_in":"","redo_booking_before_arrival":"","redo_booking_departure_info":"","redo_booking_itinerary":"","redo_booking_duration_text":"","redo_booking_important_info":"🚶‍♂️ Ngaro Track – Essential Transfer Information:
You must make your own arrangements to get to and from the start and end points of the Ngaro Track.
Please ensure you:
Confirm your marine transfer times before travelling, as access varies with tides and weather.
Arrive early for all departures and pick-ups — operators are often unable to wait due to tidal and safety constraints.
Understand that missing your scheduled transfer may result in needing to remain on the island overnight. Always carry extra food and water in case of delays.
Confirm all booking details directly with your chosen operator before travelling to ensure a smooth connection at both ends of the walk.
A permission for the park entry is essential for the walk, if you do not have this permission you may be refused transfer on the vessel.
Scamper Island Camping Transfer – What You Need to Know:
🎟 CAMP PERMIT REQUIRED:
A National Park Camp Permit is required for all overnight stays.
Rangers patrol the islands regularly.
Book your permit here: Queensland Parks Booking
🔥 IMPORTANT RULES:
Open fires are NOT permitted on any Queensland National Park islands or beaches.
Glass items are NOT allowed on the vessel.
No beach trolleys – these are unsafe onboard and not permitted.
King swags incur extra charges and must be pre-approved. They may be refused if not declared, as the vessel has limited space.
If you plan to fish, please check zoning areas and reef closures via GBRMPA:
https://www2.gbrmpa.gov.au/access/zoning/eye-on-the-reef-app
💧 Water & Transfers:
Scamper provides 5L of water per person per night, issued in jerry cans at check-in.
Once dropped at your campsite, you are fully responsible for your safety and setup.
Scamper does not provide on-island support after drop-off.
🧳 GEAR LIMITS (Per Approx. 2 People):
Recommended:
Small dome tent
Sleeping bags & mats
55L cooler or esky
Dry food container
Gas stove & utensils
Snorkel gear
Insect repellent / sunscreen (reef-safe preferred)
Eco soap & washing bucket
Clothes, walking shoes
Chairs optional (picnic tables often available at campsites)
Note: If your gear exceeds the above, please contact us in advance — extra fees may apply.
❌ NOT ALLOWED / RESTRICTED:
King-size swags (unless pre-arranged)
Beach trolleys
Excessive gear not disclosed at booking
Open flames (gas stoves permitted)
Glass bottles
Non-eco cleaning products
🛶 Want a Kayak?:
Organise directly with Salty Dog Sea Kayaking:
📧 info@saltydog.com.au
Kayak transfers incur a $20 surcharge (limited space available).
🧯 Safety & Sustainability:
Bring a first aid kit and sufficient food and water.
Use environmentally friendly products.
All rubbish must be taken back to the mainland — help us protect the islands.
Download the Eye on the Reef app for marine life info, closures, and wildlife sightings.
✈️ Looking for More Adventure?:
Take a 60-minute Scenic Flight over Heart Reef, Whitehaven Beach, and the Whitsundays.
Multiple departures daily.
Book here.
💬 Questions? Want to Book More Tours?:
Bundle activities for discounts — contact our team for assistance.
📞 Contact Us:
📧 Email: info@whitsundaycamping.com.au
📱 Phone: 0487 226 737

A: If you have dietary requirements that are generally more common i.e. lactose intolerant, vegetarian, gluten free, allergic to nuts or shellfish etc, we will advise the restaurant and they will cater to your specific requirements.

If you have requirements that are little more uncommon, please advise us in advance so we can liaise with the restaurant to confirm your requirements.

Q: Where will I be dropped off? A: Where we picked you up.

Please note that this is not including your transfers to and from your pick up location.
Q: Is there a minimum number of people to run the tour? A: We require a minimum of eight (8) people to run this tour. If your selected date does not have the required minimum, we will contact you to move your booking to an alternative date of your choosing.
Q: Will the Hunter Valley wine tour still run if the weather is bad? Can we reschedule our tour? A: We are not weather dependent for our tours and therefore will always operate. {"redo_booking_notes":"To save your valuable holiday time or time from your ABC Reef Reef Safari please complete the Pre Arrival Waiver which will be sent to you shortly.","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"","redo_booking_check_in":"","redo_booking_before_arrival":"","redo_booking_departure_info":"","redo_booking_itinerary":"","redo_booking_duration_text":"","redo_booking_important_info":"Important Information:
Medical info:
While certified divers are required to fill out the medical form on-board as well, their certification status allows them a bit more leeway in determining their medical fitness to dive. Certified divers (divers with a licence) generally need to be able to answer the following questions:
Since completing your last dive medical assessment, have you suffered any illness or injury that may affect your ability to dive safely?
Are you currently suffering any illness or injury?
Are you currently taking any prescription medication, other than the contraceptive pill?
Certified divers are generally allowed to dive if they can answer “no” to the first two questions. If they are taking prescription medication, they are generally okay to dive if they were taking it while they were doing their course or have had an updated medical.
Example if you have not dived for a few years and you are taking medication (especially if it is for anxiety, high blood pressure or anything else relating to heart /lungs) you would not be able to scuba dive in Queensland until a dive doctor has put in writing FIT TO DIVE.
We cannot refund if it turns out on the dive day that you suffer from a condition incompatible with diving and you fail to bring a clear to dive confirmation from an accredited dive doctor.
View Australian Dive Doctors.pdf (https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/frW9Ab8aTwyWWpB0f1Zz)
What to bring:
A towel, sunglasses, hat, swimmers and a change of clothes, dive log book and your certification card (if you are a certified diver).
Sunscreen:
Sunscreen is found to be damaging the reef, coral are very sensitive to chemical additives found in conventional sunscreen, which is why we recommend you to cover yourself with clothes. However, Reef and skin friendly sunscreen with no harmful additives is available at our shop.
Keep Warm & Protected:
If you suffer from the cold or prefer to have your own personal under garment, we have a variety at our shop. We provide: Good humour and all snorkel/dive equipment, lycra (stinger/rash guard suits) or wet suits, buffet lunch, tea/coffee, fruit and cakes & water.
Seasickness?
If you are not sure prevention is better than cure.
We recommend TRAVACALM (Pink&white box), a non drowsy medication available at most chemists in Australia. Take medication 1 hour before boat departure (otherwise medication won’t work). Please read more about it here. (https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/1mPlz4jR0ajaS6pfIaXu)
Meeting Location:

{"redo_booking_notes":"","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"WHAT TO WEAR AND BRING:
Wear comfortable clothes as for hiking, i.e. long pants and sturdy shoes that will keep your feet warm and dry in the wet grass (not high heels or sandals).
It will not be any colder in the air than on the ground. Dress in layers, so that you can take a jacket or jumper off, so as not to become too warm in the balloon. We suggest you bring a cap as it can get warm on your head, underneath the 'burner'. Sunglasses are also recommended.
Cameras are welcome. Personal belongings should be kept a minimum and are taken on board at your own risk.

{"redo_booking_notes":"Dear Patron,

Thank you for booking your journey on The Seaside Explorer, a heritage train experience on the Bellarine Railway. We’re excited to welcome you aboard for a day out by rail — travelling between Drysdale & Queenscliff

Ticket Information:
Your booking includes either a return or one-way journey, as selected at the time of purchase.
Return passengers will travel from Drysdale to Queenscliff and back on the same day.
One-way passengers are responsible for arranging their own transport at the opposite end of the line (Drysdale or Queenscliff).
Please double-check your ticket details prior to travel to ensure your plans match your booking.

Locomotive Information:
The Seaside Explorer may be hauled by either a steam or heritage diesel locomotive, depending on weather and operating conditions. Both are genuine historic engines from our collection, and each provides a unique experience.","redo_booking_highlights":"Your adventure begins at your selected Station, where you’ll be greeted by our friendly volunteers in traditional heritage uniforms. Take some time to explore the station and view the beautifully restored train before boarding your carriage.

Once aboard, your train will set off on a 45–55 minute journey through the Bellarine countryside — passing rolling hills, trestle bridges, farmland, and forest, following the Swan Bay shoreline.

At Queenscliff, you’ll have around two hours to explore the seaside town. Enjoy lunch, browse the local shops, or take a walk along the beach before rejoining the train for the relaxing return trip to Drysdale.","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"","redo_booking_check_in":"Your booking details and seating will be confirmed on arrival at the Drysdale Station Office, where you’ll collect your souvenir cardboard ticket before boarding.

{"redo_booking_notes":"The Program:
1. PADI ELearning: Before starting your Practical sessions however you will need to complete your PADI E-Learning. You can do this from home in your spare time as it suits you. You will need to allow 8 to 10 hours to complete it all. It is made up of short videos and questions for you to answer.
2. The Practical:
DAY 1: Your Open Water program generally starts at the SHOP at the start time indicated. You will meet your instructor, go through some theory, learn about Gear set up and how to put together your Diving Kit, and then head out to the pool to complete the confined water, skill development session.
DAY 2: We will take you out shore diving. The exact timing of the day will be discussed with you on Day 1, but you will need to allow at most 6 hours for the shore dives.
DAY 3: Is the final day of the course, this day will focus on boat diving, you can expect to be spending around 5 hours out on the boat for the last 2 dives of the course.
We usually send the PADI E-Learning (the theory) out to you a few weeks before the course. We do need you to complete it before you can hit the ocean, but we don't want you to do it too soon or you will forget everything before starting the practical.
E-Learning is a great way to learn the theory as you can do it in your own time. Don't worry though, there will be plenty of time to go over things during the course, if you have any questions, keep notes and talk to your instuctor about them.
Keep an eye out on your personal email for anything from PADI as your E-Learning, liability forms and other information will be sent to you directly from them, you will also need to electronically complete a Medical Questionaire and download a photo for your PADI E-Card.

A: Our tour goes behind the scenes on a production tour of a winery. Closed to shoes are a requirement of entry to this locations

Q: What is included in my public Hunter Valley wine tour? A: Included in your public wine tour will be transportation to and from your pick up location (choose from 2 locations in Sydney/multiple locations in the Hunter Valley), three wineries, lunch, the distillery, cheese and chocolate sampling.

Q: I have allergies/dietary requirements. Will this be catered for? A: If you have dietary requirements that are generally more common ie lactose intolerant, vegetarian, gluten free, allergic to nuts or shellfish etc, we will advise the restaurant and they will cater to your specific requirements.

If you have requirements that are little more uncommon, please advise us in advance so we can liaise with the restaurant to confirm your requirements.

We will always try our best to cater for all dietary requirements. No request is too big or too small. If you are unsure, please contact us for further details.

Q: What wineries do we go to on a public Hunter Valley wine tour? A: We have partnerships with many of Hunter Valley's finest boutique wineries. Each day can vary with the cellar doors we visit. If you would like to know the exact wineries for your tour, please call us within a week of your departure date.

Q: What time do we get back to my pick up location? A: The approximate time will be 4:30pm. Please note the time will vary due to traffic conditions and variables out of our control.

Q: Where will I be dropped of? A: Wher we picked you up.

Please note that this is not including your transfers to and from your pick up location.

Q: Is there a minimum number of people to run the tour? A: We require a minimum of eight (8) people to run this tour. If your selected date does not have the required minimum, we will contact you to move your booking to an alternative date of your choosing.

Q: Will the Hunter Valley wine tour still run if the weather is bad? Can we reschedule our tour? A: We are not weather dependent for our tours and therefore will always operate. You are mainly indoors in the warmth and comfort of a winery in the cooler months. In the warmer months, you may have the opportunity to have your wine tasting provided outdoors in the fresh air.","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":"Omitted greeting: Thank you for booking with Dave's Travel Group!"}

We are looking forward to exploring Sydney and talking architecture with you!
Please arrive 10 minutes early and don’t forget to bring your camera and your bike.

{"redo_booking_notes":"Kia Ora,

Thank you for booking with us at Dunedin Railway Station. We’re excited to welcome you on your upcoming scenic train tour from Ōamaru to Dunedin.

No need to print anything - Download your ticket from this email.

Seating is allocated - You will receive your seating details when you check in.

Ramps are available for boarding, and all carriages have toilet facilities.

Onboard Café by Precinct:
If the onboard café is operating, you’ll find fresh, locally made food produced by the award-winning Precinct team plus a range of beverages, including hot, cold and alcoholic. View menu here (https://firebrand-assets.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/DunedinRailways/Menu/Precinct+Food+Onboard+Menu+2526+Season.pdf).

Luggage & Storage:
Unfortunately, we don’t have the facilities to store your luggage at the station. Check out our friends at the Municipal Lane public convenience centre (https://help.intercity.co.nz/hc/en-us/articles/115002136748-Can-I-store-my-luggage-at-one-of-your-bus-stops) (behind the Dunedin iSITE).

Share Your Journey:
We love seeing your photos - be sure to tag @DunedinRailStation for a chance to be featured on our channels.

{"redo_booking_notes":"Join the Lady Knox Geyser Presentation - One Presentation Per Day!

Experience the incredible Lady Knox Geyser, which is located before the visitor centre.
There is only one presentation daily, starting promptly at 10:15 AM.
Don't miss this unique opportunity to witness this natural spectacle! and arrive by 9:45 AM by following the directions here to the Lady Knox parking (https://maps.app.goo.gl/ipcj3iMrcUHThSW3A)

With this ticket, if you wish, you can also go directly to the Lady Knox Geyser presentation, and after the presentation, you will be able to drive to the Waiotapu Thermal Wonderland Park and explore at your leisure.

Following the presentation, our team will direct you to the nearest parking area close to the visitor centre, from where you will access Waiotapu Thermal Wonderland Park.

Please note, there are no bathroom facilities at the Lady Knox site","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"DIRECTIONS:
From Rotorua: Travel south along the Thermal Explorer Highway (SH 5) towards Taupo for 27km (20 mins drive) until you reach the Waiotapu Tavern. Turn left opposite the tavern and travel 2km to reach Waiotapu Thermal Wonderland.
From Taupo: Travel north along the Thermal Explorer Highway (SH 5) towards Rotorua for 53km (40 mins drive). Turn right where signposted and travel a further 1km to Wai-O-Tapu Thermal Wonderland.
SHUTTLE AND INTERCITY:
Shuttle enquiries: Book a shuttle service with Rotorua i-SITE to Waiotapu Thermal Wonderland.
1167 Fenton Street, Rotorua
Email: info@rotoruanz.com
Phone: (07) 348 5179
Intercity Bus: Phone: (07) 348 0366
PARKING:
There is ample parking at the Lady Knox Geyser site, with most parks within approximately 100 metres of the arena.

{"redo_booking_notes":"","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"","redo_booking_check_in":"","redo_booking_before_arrival":"","redo_booking_departure_info":"","redo_booking_itinerary":"","redo_booking_duration_text":"","redo_booking_important_info":"Here’s what you need to know:
GETTING THERE: Start time.: Please arrive at least 5 - 10 minutes prior to the scheduled tour time. For the benefit of all guests, we start our tours on time. If you think you're going to be late, please message us on Whatsapp on +61 490 362 896 so we can make plans for you to join us. If you're more than 10 minutes late, you've missed the tour.
MEETING POINT: We start outside the southern entrance of the Queen Victoria Building. At this end there are 2 statues, one of Queen Victoria and one of a talking dog (we'll explain later). This is the Google map link (https://goo.gl/maps/tyHJVBJfbJiXUpTW9) and this is a photo of the start location (https://bit.ly/tuesmeetingspotcbd).
What to look for.: Your guide will be wearing a shirt or cap with "Local Sauce Tours" on it. It is your responsibility to approach your guide, they will be exactly where the notes say above.
Parking.: It should probably go without saying, but we don't recommend driving to the start of this tour!
Public transport.: All of our routes start and finish within close distance of train stations and bus stops. Message us if you need more details, although Google Maps is much smarter than us.
WHAT YOU SHOULD BRING: Photo identification.: In Sydney, some bars will always check ID, regardless of your age. Accepted forms of photo ID are your passport or drivers licence (overseas drivers licences are fine). Photos on your phone are not accepted, it must be physical ID.
Spending money.: We recommend bringing some cash as well as a credit card for additional food and drink purchases.
Comfortable shoes.: Over 3 hours, our route covers around 1.5 kms, so wear comfy shoes. For ladies, stylish sandals are okay, but guys require closed-in shoes. No need for heels!
Not an entirely empty belly.: We recommend that you eat before the experience. Otherwise, food is generally available at some of the bars we visit (but don't expect to be ordering a full meal).
FINAL THINGS YOU SHOULD KNOW: We run tours, rain or shine. If it’s looking a bit rainy, bring your umbrella, grab your poncho, and get ready to have fun. In very rare cases where there is extreme weather, we will be in touch with you. Assume a tour is going ahead unless you hear from us.
Contacting you.: If you have an international number and do not use WhatsApp, we will not be able to contact you if you are late/lost. If you have any issues on the day, the best way to contact us is to send us a WhatsApp message on +61 490 362 896.
Tipping & gratuities.: In Australia, tipping is optional. Having said that, we encourage our guides to go above and beyond in providing personalised recommendations and info to make your time in Sydney amazing! If you appreciate what they do, a $10 to $20 tip per person is greatly appreciated. All guides accept cash or you can use this link (https://bit.ly/localsaucetipjar).
Need to cancel or reschedule?: If you need to cancel or reschedule, let us know via email. For a full refund, cancel at least 24 hours before the experience is scheduled to start. {"redo_booking_notes":"Your guide and cook for this adventure is Sam Mcleod","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"You should bring at least 1ltr of water per day, a change of clothes in case you get wet, a warm top in case of a cool evening, a small bag of toiletries.
Sleeping bag. (If you need one please let us know)
Space is extremely limited. Kayak openings are around 20cm so soft bags are best.
You can bring phones and Cameras but remember there is a risk as they don’t float and usually don’t work if dropped in water. For anything with a touch screen it is a good idea to have a small cloth to wipe drops from wet fingers off the screen as they can be sensed as a finger touch and make use difficult.
Anything you don’t want to get wet should be in plastic.
Paddling is a water sport so expect to get splashed.
Your feet will get wet. Footwear is strongly recommended.
The clothing Golden Rules - your kayak clothing should:
NO COTTON or DENIM - when it gets wet, it does not dry and remains cold and heavy! NOT EVEN JOCKS or socks!
When wet your clothing must stay warm AND dry quickly!
The key concept to bear in mind is layering. Several thin garments will keep you just as warm as a single thicker one, and are much more versatile. Remember you’ll need to think about staying cool as much as staying warm, and you can always add or subtract layers.
A light Nylon Jacket will keep out wind and water. Fleeces are OK. Avoid heavy Jackets","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"Sydney Kayak supplies the kayaks and kayaking equipment, Tents, sleeping mat and camping equipment, Food Drink, Wine and Beer. {"redo_booking_notes":"Thank you for booking a snorkel tour with us. We're really looking forward to taking you out and showing you why this coastline is such a special place to explore.

Depending on the conditions on the day, you might encounter some of our local favourites — cryptic nudibranchs, seahorses, and the lively kelp gardens that shelter Eden’s weedy sea dragons and curious wrasse.

It’s also common to see rays gliding along the sand, schools of fish, and the occasional octopus tucked into a rocky hideout. If we're lucky, we may even meet a friendly blue grouper or hear whales singing in the distance during migration season.

Below is some additional information to help you prepare for your tour, including forms to complete.
Sites are weather-dependent and usually 5–25 minutes away
If you have any questions, please let me know.

{"redo_booking_notes":"The session starts at 9.30am (before the Park opens at 10am) Mandy will greet you and give you access to set up in our Barbecue/Picnic area. Please ask the guests to arrive by 9.20am so we are ready to enter the Park at 9.30am. Any late comers will need to wait outside the Park (with their parent/guardian) until Mandy can go back and collect them.

Only Booked in participants will be allowed access before 10am.

Unbooked guests (parents/family) will need to pay upon entry at 10am.

The Birthday program is fairly flexible and is tailored to each group -It will include meeting, interacting and handfeeding our wide range of animals - from chickens, guinea pigs, sheep,and alpacas to quokkas, emus, koalas and kangaroos. and a very special feeding session with our very friendly rainbow lorikeets! As well as some animal related games and other fun activities.

Photos taken during the session will be available via our private Facebook Group - Urimbirra Programs. These could also feature on our social media pages - please let us know if you wish this NOT to occur.

We will arrive back to the Barbecue area at about 11.30 - and the children usually have built up an appetite! The Hosted part of the Program finishes at 11.30 - but you are more than welcome to stay on, have some lunch and go back out into the Park for another walk if you like. Children must be supervised by an adult. Please remember to be quiet and respectful around our animals - so that all will have an enjoyable time!

Don't leave any food unattended - our Kangaroos and peacocks have been known to be quite resourceful!

Parents will need to pick up their Children at your designated time. Please ask your guests parents to wait in the car park area when picking up their child There is an area to the right of the Entrance door - marked by a traffic cone- that allows space for them to gather safely - as the area inside the shop can become congested.

Parents can not enter the park to pick up their children

We would also appreciate the area being left neat and tidy - with any rubbish placed in the bins provided.

{"redo_booking_notes":"We’re excited to have you join us and want to ensure you have a safe and enjoyable time on the water. Please take a moment to read the important information below regarding your booking:

Booking Times
Please arrive on time, as bookings are scheduled to ensure smooth and efficient service for all guests.

Collection and Return Point
Kayaks and paddleboards are collected and returned at the Penneshaw Penguin Centre. Kayak trolleys are available to assist with transporting equipment to the beach (approximately 20 metres away).

Clothing and Belongings
This is a water-based activity, so please dress appropriately for getting wet. A limited number of dry bags are available to borrow; however, you are welcome to bring your own if preferred.

Safety Briefing and Restricted Areas
Upon collection, our staff will provide a map and indicate areas where kayaking and paddleboarding are not permitted for safety reasons. Please follow all guidance provided.

Wildlife and Environmental Care
We ask all paddlers to respect local marine life and nearby penguin habitats by keeping a safe distance, avoiding landing in sensitive areas, and never feeding wildlife.

Life Jackets
In accordance with South Australian marine safety laws, lifejackets must be worn at all times while on the water. We have a wide range of sizes available at the Penneshaw Penguin Centre for collection with your hire equipment, and lifejackets are included in your booking.

Liability
Participants take part at their own risk. {"redo_booking_notes":"We’re excited to have you join us and want to ensure you have a safe and enjoyable time on the water. Please take a moment to read the important information below regarding your booking:

Booking Times
Please arrive on time, as bookings are scheduled to ensure smooth and efficient service for all guests.

Collection and Return Point
Kayaks are collected and returned at the Penneshaw Penguin Centre. Kayak trolleys are available to assist with transporting equipment to the beach (approximately 20 metres away).

Clothing and Belongings
This is a water-based activity, so please dress appropriately for getting wet. A limited number of dry bags are available to borrow; however, you are welcome to bring your own if preferred.

Safety Briefing and Restricted Areas
Upon collection, our staff will provide a map and indicate areas where kayaking is not permitted for safety reasons. Please follow all guidance provided.

Wildlife and Environmental Care
We ask all paddlers to respect local marine life and nearby penguin habitats by keeping a safe distance, avoiding landing in sensitive areas, and never feeding wildlife.

Life Jackets
In accordance with South Australian marine safety laws, lifejackets must be worn at all times while on the water. We have a wide range of sizes available at the Penneshaw Penguin Centre for collection with your hire equipment, and lifejackets are included in your booking.

Liability
Participants take part at their own risk. {"redo_booking_notes":"We can't wait to share our flower farm with you through our Dahlia Field. It doesn't stop you coming - but it does mean we're a bit more prepared. Footwear is a must - we can't let you out in the field with nothing protecting your feet.

If you're an avid dahlia grower and are wanting to know the names of the dahlias in our field, please do ask - Karly loves to share and although doesn't know every single one, we've got the large majority of them named and ready to share.

One of the best parts of our experiences is being outside in our peaceful environment up close and personal with the bees, or simply wandering through the flower farm. Learn more about the Tiaki promise here - https://www.tiakinewzealand.com/en_NZ/about-tiaki/

{"redo_booking_notes":"Please be ready 10 minutes before your scheduled pickup time and ready to board the shuttle on arrival.

Having the right gear is crucial for a fun and safe walk. You need lots of warm and waterproof clothing – temperatures at the top of the track are often freezing, even when it is warm and sunny, particularly in the Mangatepopo Valley.

The track is very rough underfoot and sturdy shoes will help stop sprained ankles. Hiking boots are best.

There is very little shade, so pack a sunhat and 2-3L of water per person
Bring your lunch and lots of snacks, you can’t buy food along the track, and you’ll get hungry
Bring your own toilet paper and hand sanitiser - there’s none in the toilets.

Be prepared for a long and challenging day out.
To have a safe and enjoyable hike, you should be confident that you can:

Walk for 8 hours
Walk for 19.4 km with lots of up and down
Keep your balance on a rough track. You’ll be walking over loose rocks and gravel, including going down a steep gravel slope with no handrail or stairs
Take everything on the Day Hikes packing list including lots of warm and waterproof clothes
Cope with extreme weather, including rain and cold. The track is in an alpine environment. Freezing temperatures are common even on sunny days.","redo_booking_highlights":"","redo_booking_what_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_not_to_bring":"","redo_booking_what_included":"","redo_booking_what_excluded":"","redo_booking_extras":"","redo_booking_meeting_point":"","redo_booking_check_in":"","redo_booking_before_arrival":"","redo_booking_departure_info":"","redo_booking_itinerary":"","redo_booking_duration_text":"","redo_booking_important_info":"","redo_booking_health_safety":"","redo_booking_restrictions":"","redo_booking_special_requirements":"","redo_booking_accessibility":"","redo_booking_group_size":"","redo_booking_cancellation":"","redo_booking_disclaimers":"","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":""}

{"redo_booking_notes":"We will all meet 10 minutes before the start time at Customs House Square, which is in front of Customs House, Circular Quay. The exact meeting place is the benches under the sun awnings facing Young Street. Marked with the red arrow in the image below.

You can easily walk here from anywhere in the city, catch a train to Circular Quay Station, catch a bus to Alfred Street (such as the 333), or take the light rail to Circular Quay (the final stop).

If you are late or lost, please call Elliot on 0431922619. Your guide will be wearing a purple shirt.

Please wear good walking shoes to walk about 5km (3.1 miles). Bring water bottles and snacks. Wet weather gear if light rain is forecast. A hat and sunblock are advised as we will be outside in the sun.

We will stop around halfway at a cafe/bar, and you are welcome to purchase a coffee (even an Aperol Spritz!). We will pass a souvenir store in the Botanic Gardens next to the first restroom break. Please let the guide know in advance if you wish to visit it.

The tour ends at the Old Fitzroy Hotel in Woolloomooloo.

{"redo_booking_notes":"As you might already know the Standard PADI Open Water Course is composed of 3 sections: the pool section, the open water section and the theory.

In a separate email sent by PADI, you are going to get access to your digital material including Knowledge Review, Quizz and Final Exam. If you haven't receive your email, check your "junk folder" and contact us if you haven't got it yet. Please log as soon as you received the PADI email and complete the medical form. If you wait too long to complete it, it will be disactivated and you will have to call PADI to renew it.

If you encounter any issues with the elearning, please call PADI directly: 02 9454 2888

In this email you will find a link to the PADI videos. Watch them, while you are doing the knowledge reviews. At the end of each section, complete the quiz and finish with the final exam. All must be completed before the course.

{"redo_booking_notes":"We look forward to taking you on our beekeeper experience journey soon, a few health and safety notes for the day!

Wearing closed shoes is a must. If you feel anxious around bees, the best advice is to wear an extra layer, you'll be well protected in our bee suits, but long pants and tops will always protect you further, and plus - it's much easier to get into your bee suit in shorts or pants than it is in a skirt or dress! There's always the chance of getting stung so if you know you're allergic please let us know before you head out so we can ensure we've got measures in place to keep you safe.

We're really looking forward to sharing our passion of all things bees and honey with you - if you've got any burning questions make sure you remember to ask us, a tour is always more exciting if you engage with us.

One of the best parts of our experiences is being outside in our peaceful environment up close and personal with the bees, or simply wandering through the flower farm. {"redo_booking_notes":"A few things to make your trip easier and set expectations. We have to get everyone ready before hand so;

PLEASE BE AT THE SHOP 45 min BEFORE DEPARTURE.

There will be a bit of standing around as we go through everyone's needs but we will try to make the process as quick as possible.

You will be out on the boat for between 4 to 5 hours, we will have sunscreen, fresh water, biscuits, tea, coffee, hot chocolate and soup for the trip, but if you want anything else you should bring it with you.

Also remember to keep hydrated and use sun protection out on the water.

After we get back feel free to come back up to the shop to record the dives or just have a chat about what has gone on.

We are a SEA SHEPHERD DIVE CENTER (https://divejervisbay.com/environmental-policy/) so we don't support any behaviour that will negatively impact on the Marine Life on our trips and everywhere that we dive is part of the Marine Park.

{"redo_booking_notes":"This journey normally starts at the airport, cruise port or hotel in city. It is generally a 6 hour excursion with customised sightseeing on the way to and from Opuke Hot Pools in Methven.

We will usually go through the Rakaia Gorge, a destination in itself famous for Jet Boat Tours, hiking, fishing & relaxation. For locals it is a great way to take advantage of the swim up bar and have a get together with out the hassle of driving home.

Experience the ultimate rejuvenation in naturally heated pools surrounded by stunning Selwyn landscapes. Whether you’re looking to unwind after an adventure or simply enjoy a peaceful soak, these thermal waters offer the perfect retreat.

{"redo_booking_notes":"This course has been designed around an expedition along the Western Australian Coast where you will be part of a working crew, participating in all the skills you need to become a competent yachts person.
You will be trained to take over command of the yacht and by the end of the course should be able to handle the vessel safely and competently.
You will be studying an IYT sailing course and graduate with an internationally recognized certificate that will allow you to charter yachts around the world.
We will also fit in plenty of adventure including swimming, snorkelling, fishing, exploring and friendship.

Check our website to learn more about our sailing catamaran Queimarla (https://www.adventuresailing.com.au/catamaran-queimarla). She is a 45ft high performance sailing machine which is fully certified by AMSA (Australian Maritime Safety Authority)
Your captain/instructor Captain Paul (https://www.adventuresailing.com.au/the-team) is a fully qualified professional skipper (Master 45m) with over 35 years sailing experience. Few people know the coast as well as him. You can rest assured that you will be in safe hands on a very sea worthy vessel!

There are 3 courses that can be completed during a 5-day course. The one you study will depend on your experience and your training needs.
Option 1. International Crew Certificates (3 day summer trips): This course has NO prerequisites.
Minimum age 16.
This course is often chosen if folks require less training, therefore allowing more time for relaxing and enjoying the environment. (Less work more play)
This is a good introductory level, covering all the skills required to sail a large catamaran safely & competently.
More information on this course HERE (https://www.iytworld.com/courses/international-crew-training/)
Option 2. International Flotilla Skipper (5 day winter trips): You must hold a Marine Radio licence before the issue of this certificate. (This can be done on board during your course.)
Minimum age 16 years old.
This is a high-level training course with the aim of skilling you to be able to take command of a vessel up to 24m.
This certificate will allow you to charter yachts.
This qualification can be converted to an ICC cert to use for chartering yachts in Europe (cost $150)
These courses are conducted along the WA coast between Busselton & the Abrolhos Islands.
More information on this course HERE (https://www.iytworld.com/courses/international-flotilla-skipper/)
Option 3 International Bareboat Skipper: VHF radio licence required.
Must have completed 200 nm and 10 days at sea (By the end of the course) to qualify for this qualification.
This qualification can be converted to an ICC certificate to use for chartering yachts in Europe. (cost $150)
More information on this course HERE (https://www.iytworld.com/courses/international-bareboat-skipper/)

Please note. The only shower onboard is a manual deck shower. Saltwater soap is provided.

Suggestions to help you study for your course onboard.
International crew for 3 day courses
International bareboat skipper for 5 day courses
Vhf short range certificates for radio licence.

A: We can offer you, at the successful passing of the exam, 3 qualifications at the end of this course. International Yacht Training, International bareboat skippers’ qualification.
International certificate of competency http://www.iytworld.com
Short range operators’ certificate of proficiency. (VHF radio Licence)
Q: Is there any online training available prior to joining Queimarla? A: We will provide you with a comprehensive “e course” that you can work through in the comfort of your own home prior to sailing with us.
You will also receive an “e copy” of the IYT textbook for your course.
We will also send you a series of links to online u tube clips that we think are knowledgeable and worth watching.
Q: What is your rough weather contingency plan? A: We place your safety above all other considerations.
Queimarla is a remarkable sea boat that has successfully sailed around the world. She is strong, safe and is fully approved by AMSA. We do not take undue risk; however, we do not hide from a little rough weather. This is your opportunity to stretch your envelope of comfort whilst having a lifelong professional sailor onboard with you.
Saying this we can fly home from the Abrolhos Islands if caught out there by extreme weather.
Q: Can we fish onboard? A: This is predominately a sailing trip, but we certainly tow a lure when able and have a fish at anchor. We do not bring fish home; we eat what we catch onboard. You must make sure you have a current WA Recreational Fishing license (https://www.fish.wa.gov.au/Fishing-and-Aquaculture/Recreational-Fishing/Pages/Recreational-Fishing-Licences.aspx) if you wish to spear fish, dive for crays or fish.
Q: Can we surf? A: We have no insurance for surfing.
Q: What about Diving? A: We would be crazy not to enjoy this incredible environment into which we are sailing. Yes, to snorkelling, yes to insurance, yes to we have gear onboard.
Q: What gear is onboard? A: All safety gear including life jackets & harnesses.
All bedding.
All Food and cooking equipment.
Fridge & Freezer.
Sunscreen.
Snorkelling gear
SUP board.
3.75m dinghy.
Basic fishing gear.
2 x SUP boards & paddles.
All training resources and equipment.
Blue tooth speaker.
Manual deck shower only
Salt water soap.
Q: Do we need to study? A: We get 3 different sorts of people onboard: Those that want the awesome experience, those that want to be able to sail a charter boat and need the qualifications and those that want to sail their own boats and adventures.
Which are you? The last two groups should do some pre-study as provided. This will deepen your learning. The first group can mix another piña colada and observe!
Q: Do I have to get the certificates? A: IYT charge $150 per certificate. You need them if chartering, they may reduce your insurance premium or make insurance easier to get and they look great in the pool room, but the choice is yours.
Q: Is there a hot shower? A: We spend a great deal of effort keeping water out of the boat, so there is no shower below decks. We do have a saltwater deck shower, saltwater soap available and a freshwater rinse down on deck. We try to swim every day and so far, we have had no complaints about our smell.
Please DO NOT bring baby wipes or body wipes. These things are an environmental disaster and the most prevalent blockers of marine toilets ever invented. They should be illegal.
Swimming in the blue ocean is a perfect way to stay clean and fresh. We will have biodegradable salt water soap that works a treat.
Q: What is the food like? A: I really like food. Lots of delicious fresh food. You will eat well and be part of the crew preparing these delicious meals. This can get a little competitive and result in some spectacular outcomes. You won’t be disappointed.
Q: How do we get to the boat? A: We mostly sail from Fremantle, Busselton, and Port Denison (Dongara). Travel to the boat is your responsibility. Some folk drive, some catch the Trans West bus. (Cheap and efficient) We have no secure parking available in Dongara. However, we have never had an issue. Yet.
Q: Coffee and Tea? A: We will have a selection of teas available on board, and fresh coffee beans. We have a hand crank coffee grinder, plungers and an Aeropress. It's a coveted job grinding the morning brew whilst standing up on deck staring at the water!","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":"Omitted greeting/sign-off line: Thank you for booking your sailing adventure with us... we are looking forward to sailing with you and helping you achieve your sailing dreams!"}
