Aotearoa New Zealand: Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years. Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.
Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes, landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes. Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand the risks, before you go.
Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland. We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or disrupt your visit.
Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides. These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But they will happen again.
The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in the next 50 years (find out more at af8.org.nz (https://af8.org.nz/)). An earthquake of this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.
What to do in an earthquake: DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less likely you are to be injured.
Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
For more detailed information, please visit Emergency Management Southland (https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or AF8 (https://af8.org.nz/).","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"Contact Us: For enquiries about your reservation, please contact the RealNZ team on contact@realnz.com (mailto:contact@realnz.com) or 0800 65 65 01 (tel:08006565010). {"redo_booking_notes":"The day will be broken up into 3 parts; Surfing, Surf Fitness & Surf Yoga:

Step out into nature, feel the breeze of the ocean on your skin and your toes melting into the sand as you embark on your journey towards a healthier, fitter and more relaxed version of yourself with our Women Surf, Yoga & Wellness Day.

“Women Surf & Wellness Day “ looks at combining women’s passion for the ocean, adventure and being active, with a relaxing, holistic and healthy living approach to surfing through yoga. We strive to lure women away from their stressful, everyday lives and into the surf for one incredible, revitalising day!

FITNESS: Strong it’s the new sexy!
Our Surf Fitness class will focus upon basic fitness concepts, body strength, flexibility and balance, all of which are applied during surfing. We encourage all levels of fitness to join in and encourage individuals to train at a pace they feel comfortable. The environment will be a very positive, supportive one; we are all on a journey of healthier living together.

SURFING: Let the Ocean set you free!
Whether you are an experienced surfer or it’s your first time in the water, our instructors will cater to your specific needs, teaching you the basics of turning, paddling and getting up on your board, or improving your already existing skills.

Choose your level:

Beginner Surf Lesson (Level 1): For those that are new to surfing, or never surfed before. Also for those that may have had a few surf lessons before but are still working on the basics, like your popup, Paddling, getting your weight forward on the board and riding. This includes:
Beach awareness, safety, and session plan
Know your board
Ocean entry and board handling
The mount, positioning & paddling
Whitewater gliding & manoeuvring
The popup to surf stance methods
Speed & manoeuvring

Progressive Improver Lesson (Level 2): For those who are constantly popping up and riding broken whitewater and the occasional unbroken green wave. This includes:
Beach awareness, safety, and session plan
Beginner refresher, understanding your board and the waves
Positioning & trimming
Paddling for success
The glide & popup
Compressions / extension for speed – the why, when, how
Frontside & backside turns
Bottom turns

YOGA: Breath & Recover
Similar to the surfing, whether you're a veteran yogi or have never been to a class, our yoga teacher will be sure to tailor the class to all levels. It will encompass gentle movements, stretches and breathing techniques, all of which interrelate to the movements made whilst surfing. Presence, mindfulness and awareness, body alignment and connection, breathing and energy flow are all vital components of our everyday lives that will be explored throughout the class.

Know your board

{"redo_booking_notes":"Precis of Queensland cycling rules and safety:
RULES:
PATHWAYS:
Shared pathways: Keep Left, ring bell to warn of passing pedestrians
Cyclists give way to people, slow down
Separate pathways: Cyclists use the side of the pathway indicated by the sign
Bicycle only:
For bicycles only
You can use any speed
On-road bicycle lanes.: You must follow all road rules
You are sharing the road with other vehicles
Keep as far left as possible
NO Bicycle zone: You must dismount and walk your bike
DO NOT RIDE IN PUBLIC SQUARES, WALK YOUR BIKE.
RIDING:
Keep at two hands on handlebars unless giving signals.
Have one leg on each side of the seat.
Face forward.
To signal RIGHT-TURN, extend arm out horizontally with hand open, palm facing forward. To signal STOP, raise arm with elbow bent at right angle and hand up with palm facing forward.
One person per bike unless the bike is designed as a tandem bike.
Keep two meters from the back of a vehicle when following.
DO NOT ride into the path of a driver or pedestrian.
Keep left at all times.
Do not overtake another vehicle on the left if that vehicle is indicating and turning left.
Do not ride more than two abreast.
If riding beside another rider, ride no more than 1.5m apart.
For a more comprehensive list of rules go to https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/safety/rules/wheeled-devices/bicycle
IF YOU BREAK THE ROAD RULES YOU MAY BE FINED. THERE IS NO AGE LIMIT FOR BEING FINED.
SAFETY:
Wear your helmet and enclosed shoes
Cycle at appropriate speed.
Go slow when there are people about.
Ring the bell when approaching pedestrians, dogs, etc.
Keep left at all times.
Use appropriate lights and reflectors in low light level situations and at night.
REVIEW FULL SAFETY INFORMATION HERE: https://www.ecotekk.com.au/home/ecotekk-e-bike-safety/

Aotearoa New Zealand: Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years. Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.
Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes, landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes. Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand the risks, before you go.
Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland. We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or disrupt your visit.
Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides. These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But they will happen again.
The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in the next 50 years (find out more at af8.org.nz) (https://af8.org.nz/). An earthquake of this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.
What to do in an earthquake: DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less likely you are to be injured.
Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
For more detailed information, please visit Emergency Management Southland (https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or AF8 (https://af8.org.nz/).","redo_booking_pricing":"","redo_booking_faqs":"","redo_booking_contact":"","redo_booking_flags":""}

In preparation for your upcoming Recreational Skipper ticket course (https://www.transport.wa.gov.au/imarine/recreational-skippers-ticket.asp) you are required to obtain some paperwork to meet the Department of Transport requirements.

Please select your appropriate group.

Over 18 with drivers licence: You simply bring your WA drivers licence with you on the day of your course.

Under 18 with drivers licence or learners permit: You will need your licence or learners permit with this parent consent form (https://www.transport.wa.gov.au/mediaFiles/marine/MAC_F_ProFormaLetterOfConsent.pdf).

Under 18 NO LICENCE or Learners Permit

These are small parcels of wine that can stand amongst the finest wines from anywhere. The wines reflect Philip's philosophy on wine making; select an exceptional site and the right varieties. Marry the vineyard and the winemaking.

Philip Shaw's Hoosegg wines are made with the lessons learnt from the past 60 years of winemaking; elegant, vibrant, intense and complex. They are wines that all wine lovers, will relish.

{"redo_booking_notes":"We look forward to hosting a fun day out full of adventure, nature & an indulgent lunch.
Your first stop for the day will be Thunderbird Park, where you'll kick-start the day with a 3 hour TreeTop challenge. The TreeTop Challenge at Tamborine Mountain is Australia’s largest High Ropes Adventure Park with more than 120 TreeTop Activities, including 10 flying foxes! These courses range from easy to extreme and traverse through 9 acres of amazing bushland and rainforest. The adventure park is designed for all fitness levels and ages (from 8 years and over).
Please wear appropriate closed shoes & have your phones in a zipped pocket (or stored away before you embark on your TreeTop Challenge).
After an adventure packed morning, it's time to reward yourself with an indulgent winery lunch at the top of Mt Tamborine. Here, we'll start with a delicious wine tasting, followed by a delectable two-course lunch.
If you have selected the full day itinerary, we will finish the day off with a second wine or liqueur tasting before making our way back to your drop-off point.

{"redo_booking_notes":"If travelling from Taupo to Turangi allow drive time at least one and a half hours travel with no road work AND make sure to take HWY 1.

Turn right onto Volcanic Loop Hwy/State Hwy 46 (signs for National Park).
https://maps.app.goo.gl/eSCoprFdCySihjCB9

It will take 15-20 minutes approximately 12.6 km to get to the car park once you are on HWY46 road. The actual sign is on the right side of the road and says 'TONGARIRO SHUTTLE CAR PARK'.
https://maps.app.goo.gl/Ck66FBjBEc3rpAAD6

TRAVELLING FROM NATIONAL PARK VILLAGE you will take HWY 47. Which is directly across from the G.A.S Petrol Station
https://maps.app.goo.gl/Xp5i5FcTsJ9a3daJA

Travel that road 26.6 km approximately 25 to 30 minutes then turn right onto HWY 46
https://maps.app.goo.gl/5XZVqEc9UFAQXjug6

It will take 10 minutes approximately 6.5 km to get to the car park from there.
https://maps.app.goo.gl/j2NzKJ6S3s3G9Jv9A

You will also pass by vehicles that are parked on the side of the road. Do not do that.
You will pass by the Ketetahi track entrance sign. 400 meters to the car park.

You must be at the car park no later than 15 minutes prior to departure time. The staff of the car park will meet and check you in. Show your confirmation.

NOTE: We have five whanau (family) operators that transport out of this car park. We help each other transfer our passengers to the start of the Tongariro Alpine Crossing. You will board the first bus/shuttle that is in front of the queue. All passengers line up in an orderly manner and you will board the vehicles accordingly.
